dimensions.assessment: Affects agricultural producers and owners of nonindustrial private forest land impacted by natural disasters or eligible wildfires.
dimensions.evidence: expand eligibility for payments to agricultural producers and owners of forest land impacted by natural disasters

dimensions.assessment: Provides substantial direct financial flexibility by increasing advance payment percentages to up to 75% and extending spending timeframes to 180 days.
dimensions.evidence: Producers may receive an advance on cost-sharing payments for 75% of the cost of the replacement and 50% of the cost of the repair or restoration.

dimensions.assessment: Changes the timing and maximum percentages of advance cost-sharing payments but does not state total appropriation amounts.
dimensions.evidence: not more than 75 percent of the cost of the emergency measures

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Agricultural Credit Act of 1978 to modify rules for two specific emergency assistance programs.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Agricultural Credit Act of 1978 to remove barriers to agricultural producers in accessing funds

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory changes to the Emergency Conservation Program and Emergency Forest Restoration Program.

missing_information: Total federal outlays or overall budget impact of increasing advance payment percentages.
importance_detail.rationale: The law expands eligibility and advance payment options under the Emergency Conservation Program and Emergency Forest Restoration Program for agricultural producers and forest landowners impacted by specific natural disasters and wildfires.

card.summary: S. 1462, the Fix Our Forests Act, aims to improve forest management activities on National Forest System land, public land under the Bureau of Land Management, and Tribal land to reduce wildfire risks and return resilience to overgrown, fire-prone areas. The bill establishes programs, interagency centers, and streamlined procedures for hazardous fuels reduction, prescribed burning, reforestation, community protection, litigation reforms, and disaster assistance for wildland firefighters.
